data.body:
TRIAGE COMPLETE -- classification: genuine defect. Reproducible on current origin/main (7d3907101dd6), not fixed since filing, and contradicted by an ACCEPTED ADR rather than supported by one.

MECHANISM -- a dead conjunct. At src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py:262-267, line 262 already excludes every structural container via parent_ids_with_children (built at :162). Line 265's guard 'ttype == "story" and tid not in parent_ids_with_children' is therefore reachable ONLY when the ticket has no children, so its second conjunct is dead and the branch reduces to 'type == story => never schedulable'. The rendered reason at :405-407, 'needs implementation planning (story has 0 children)', asserts an inference nothing verifies: the branch never consults plan-review state, so a childless story holding a CURRENT CERTIFIED plan-review PASS still reports as unplanned.

THE ASYMMETRY FALSIFIES THE 'STORIES ARE CONTAINERS' READING. Under one epic, with only ticket_type varying:
  batch          : b_leaf(bug), e_leaf(epic), t_kid(task), t_leaf(task)
  needs_planning : s_leaf(story)
A childless EPIC is batched. A childless BUG is batched. Only a childless STORY is vetoed.

PRIOR ART CUTS AGAINST THE CURRENT BEHAVIOR. docs/adr/0078-plan-review-container-leaf-scrutiny.md (Accepted) already adjudicated this exact defect class: 'Proportionate scrutiny is keyed on container (has children) vs leaf (no children), never on ticket type... The defect is that TYPE is a poor proxy for ALTITUDE: a childless epic behaves like a leaf, a story with children like a container.' ADR 0078 fixed it in plan-review (bug a278) and it was NEVER PROPAGATED to the scheduler. The same rule is stated in the shipped author contract (src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md:56-58), in llm/plan_review/registry.py:437,454, det_floor.py:180, and docs/plan-review-gate.md:523. No ADR and no prose in docs/ asserts the opposite for scheduling. The branch was inherited verbatim from the bash->Python port (92caa823ae17), not introduced by a decision.

THE ONLY TEXT DEFENDING IT IS AGENT COMMENTARY INFERRED FROM THE BUG. Tickets indigoid-unmystic-serpent, truthful-specified-silverfish and immune-floury-toad all carry 'Retyped from story to task after the final scheduling audit: next-batch intentionally skips childless stories as planning containers', and forcible-diminished-lamb (08ab-60d2-3082-4b47) is now ticket_type task as a result. That is not prior art supporting the design -- it is the record of what it has cost, in tickets mistyped to route around it.

SURFACE PARITY -- one gap, and it is between operations not surfaces. Within next-batch all three surfaces funnel through the single compute (CLI reads_cli.py:561, library _reads.py:204 -> next_batch_state:448, MCP _mcp_reads.py:442), so one fix covers all three. But reads.ready_states (reads.py:560) applies NO type filter, so 'ready' returns the childless story while 'next-batch' files it under skipped_needs_planning -- two operations documented as one pipeline (ready -> next-batch) disagreeing about the same ticket. AC4 closes that.

BLAST RADIUS MEASURED, not estimated: deleting lines 264-267 and running all 23 test files mentioning next-batch gives '1 failed, 405 passed'. The single failure is test_next_batch_behavior.py::test_childless_story_needs_planning -- the test that codifies the bug. No golden, no schema, no MCP model breaks.

Removing a branch LOWERS cyclomatic complexity, so the complexity ratchet reports stale and passes, and no mechanism is added.

FOLLOW-UP worth its own ticket rather than scope creep here: after the fix, skipped_needs_planning can never be non-empty. Retaining it (as this ticket chose) is the right call for compatibility given _mcp_models.py:250 and next_batch.schema.json:29, but it leaves a permanently-empty field as small maintenance debt.
